messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: PagerDuty triggered — node heartbeat lost for `infer-usw-12` (inference-pool-usw). Severity: P2. Triggered by kubelet-heartbeat-monitor (missing status for ~2m).

sara_oncall: On it. pinging infra. @mike_infra can you check node health + kubelet logs?

mike_infra: running quick checks: `kubectl get nodes | grep infer-usw-12`
```
infer-usw-12   NotReady   5m   1 GPU   8 pods
```
kubectl describe shows: Ready=False (KubeletNotReady), last heartbeat ~120s ago. Kubelet events: "failed to read node status" repeated.

mike_infra: checked dmesg on the host — lots of GPU driver entries: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid 1024` and "GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus". Also container runtime logs show several restarts of `redwood-infer-runtime` with OOMKilled.

sara_oncall: Ok cordoning + draining now to evacuate pods. running: `kubectl cordon infer-usw-12` then `kubectl drain infer-usw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m`

incident-bot: action recorded: node cordoned and drain started by sara_oncall.

javier_ops: Kicked nodepool autoscaler to +2 nodes (temp) to pick up load. Adjusting routing so inference traffic avoids infer-usw-*. Will monitor capacity.

mike_infra: SSH'd to host. tried `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` — kubelet was stuck waiting on containerd overlay lock. Restarted containerd, then kubelet. Kubelet came up but dmesg still shows periodic NVRM Xid messages. I've pulled the kernel and nvidia-driver versions — looks like a driver/kernel mismatch after the last node image rollout.

anya_sre: I'm on standby to take handoff in 30m. What's customer impact currently?

sara_oncall: Observability: inference-pool error rate spiked to ~1.3% with 503/502s and a tail latency increase (~95th percentile went from 220ms to 1.8s). After drain + autoscale, errors down to ~0.25% and p95 ~300ms. A couple customers reported elevated latency (CS tickets created: CS-4321, CS-4324). Filing follow-ups.

mike_infra: Rolling back GPU driver to known-good (535.86) now on the node image in the staging group. Will also pin driver on the affected node and restart `nvidia-modprobe`/driver.

incident-bot: update: kubelet reported Ready for infer-usw-12; pods are re-scheduling. Monitoring pod restart counts for redwood-infer-runtime.

sara_oncall: Observability shows pods transitioned and error-rate trending to baseline. Starting incident wrap checklist. Creating follow-up OPS ticket OPS-1256 with timeline and mitigation steps. Notifying support to message impacted customers via CS-4321 thread. Link to runbook included: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/node-heartbeat-flap

mike_infra: root-cause lead: kernel/driver version mismatch causing intermittent GPU driver disconnects -> container crashes/OOMs -> kubelet status flaps. Action items: pin driver on node images, add node-level dmesg alerting for NVRM Xid > threshold, validate driver post-rollout.

anya_sre: I'm taking this over. Current state: node drained, kubelet back to Ready, traffic routed away during the incident, autoscaler incremented +2, customer-facing errors largely resolved. I'll draft a short post-incident note and keep watch for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:

sara_oncall: Thanks — handing off to anya_sre. Closing the P2 if no regressions in the next 15m. :thumbsup:

anya_sre: A quick handoff summary for next oncall: infer-usw-12 experienced kernel <-> nvidia-driver mismatch after last image rollout, caused GPU disconnects and container OOMs, kubelet heartbeat stopped posting. Mitigation: cordon+drain, autoscale +2, restart containerd/kubelet, rollback/pin GPU driver, monitor. Followups: OPS-1256 (postmortem), driver pin in node image pipeline, improved dmesg alerting.
